### ASTRA-S2-R1-01 — closed (previous P2)

At `src/ui/notices.ts:35–38`, only a successful **persistence** notification resolves an existing central persistence notice. System/export success cannot establish local recovery. `src/runtime/session.ts:307–331` still confirms a current successful repository operation before acknowledging a manual write; cancelled/disposed completions cannot acknowledge a newer session. The correction neither creates a notice queue nor clears unrelated errors, hazards or the detached call.

The candidate's regression tests and my independent composition probe pass. In the retained final native-rAF trace, failed F5 and repeated failure/export preserve the journal, central failure and autosave-off reminder. Recovery is observed **264.8 ms** after the preceding failure/export observation, well before the error deadline. The error/reminder disappear; the success chip expires **3428.6 ms** later without replay. The exported state equals every field of recovered state at paused tick **14454**; the former current generation is retained verbatim as previous. A separate actual Canopy F5 keeps the warning, hazard and call visible. I inspected all corresponding final PNGs.

### SOL-S2-R1-1 — closed (previous P2)

`src/ui/panels.ts:63–70` now observes the existing anchor policy without rendering. Both panel refresh (`:81`) and `GameView.update` (`src/ui/view.ts:371–374`) invoke it. An observed departure clears From, explicit To and obsolete fallback; roster changes and bench/cradle movement within the same site do not clear valid intent. Accessibility/fallback handling remains in panel composition.

The real-GameView regression covers closed-panel updates, focus, scroll, timers, commands and unchanged state. My additional probe uses the recorded earned departure/return states, freezes the input objects, and supplies a DOM object that throws on access: 100 same-site observations retain both chosen operands; departure/return clears them and fallback without DOM access or state writes. The final trace independently establishes field departure at **13385**, inaccessible Dart, workshop return at **14398**, no panel opened/rewritten en route, unchanged inventory and no transfer submitted. Native same-site reopen retains Dart; reopening after travel defaults to Workshop locker. The screenshots visibly agree.

These findings concerned contradictory UI lifetime behavior. Neither established inventory or save corruption, and this report does not recast them as corruption fixes.
